'''Paolo Napoleon James Banchero''' (born November 12, 2002; pronounced {{IPAc-en|ˈ|p|aʊ|l|oʊ|nbsp|b|æ|n|ˈ|k|ɛər|oʊ}} {{respell|POW|loh|_|ban|KAIR|oh}}<ref>{{cite AV media|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3OuDxldBaSA|title=NBA 2K22: Paolo Banchero Gets Scanned In Game |publisher= [[NBA 2K]] |date=2022-03-18|accessdate=2022-05-19|time=0:04}}</ref>) is an Italian-American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. A projected top-3 pick in 2022, he was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2021 class. In 2022, he was named the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] Rookie of the Year.
==Early life==
Banchero reached a height of {{convert|3|ft|m|2}} at 15 months of age.<ref name="mother">{{cite web |last1=Glass |first1=Gregg |title=Flashback: Rhonda Smith Franklin, Class of 1992 |url=https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/?date=20040302&slug=flashback02 |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |access-date=April 26, 2020 |date=March 2, 2004}}</ref> In his childhood, he played basketball and [[American football]] and took part in [[track and field|track]].<ref name="egan">{{cite web |last1=Egan |first1=Chris |title=O'Dea basketball star Paolo Banchero getting national attention |url=https://www.king5.com/article/sports/high-school/prep-zone-odea-basketball-star-paolo-banchero-getting-national-attention/281-4062dd68-5018-4f91-a2ac-d93d921e2a1c |publisher=[[KING-TV]] |access-date=April 27, 2020 |date=February 13, 2020}}</ref> He grew up playing basketball at Rotary Boys and Girls Club of [[Seattle]], drawing inspiration from his mother, who played professionally. In seventh grade, Banchero grew from {{height|ft=6|in=1}} to {{height|ft=6|in=5}}.<ref name="allen">{{cite web |last1=Allen |first1=Aaron |title=Paolo Banchero's Humility And Leadership Has Led Him To A Stellar Season |url=https://seattlemedium.com/paolo-bancheros-humility-leadership-led-stellar-season/ |website=[[Seattle Medium]] |access-date=April 26, 2020 |date=February 12, 2020}}</ref> He was ranked among the top 50 eighth-graders nationally in both basketball and football.<ref name="mireporter">{{cite web |title=Mercer Island student nationally ranked in two sports |url=https://www.mi-reporter.com/sports/mercer-island-student-nationally-ranked-in-two-sports/ |website=[[Mercer Island Reporter]] |access-date=April 26, 2020 |date=May 8, 2017}}</ref>

==High school career==
In his first year at [[O'Dea High School]] in Seattle, Banchero played football, as the backup [[quarterback]] on the state championship team, as well as basketball.<ref name="bennett">{{cite web |last1=Bennett |first1=Brian |title=He goes by Paolo (Banchero), and his game may make him a household name |url=https://theathletic.com/1104436/2019/07/30/he-goes-by-paolo-banchero-and-his-game-may-make-him-a-household-name/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=April 26, 2020 |date=July 30, 2019}}</ref> As a freshman on the basketball team, he averaged 14.1 points and 10.2 rebounds per game.<ref name="divens">{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=2017-18 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Freshman All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/0qJPsGnrtk2IulXRwgDt_Q/2017-18-maxpreps-boys-basketball-freshman-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=April 27, 2020 |date=April 19, 2018}}</ref> In his sophomore season, Banchero averaged 18.2 points, 10.3 rebounds and 4.3 assists per game, leading O'Dea to the Class 3A state championship, where he was named [[most valuable player]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=2018-19 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/wCRc7AkDlUOzrgbdS9nvZA/2018-19-maxpreps-boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=April 27, 2020 |date=April 18, 2019}}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 22.6 points, 11 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.6 blocks per game for the Class 3A runners-up, earning Washington [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] and [[MaxPreps National Basketball Player of the Year awards#Junior of the Year|MaxPreps National Junior of the Year]] honors.<ref name="joyce">{{cite web |last1=Joyce |first1=Nathan |title=O'Dea's Paolo Banchero named Gatorade player of the year for Washington |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/odeas-paolo-banchero-named-gatorade-player-of-the-year-for-washington/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |access-date=April 27, 2020 |date=March 26, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=MaxPreps 2019-20 Boys Basketball Junior All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/81pLsfgvYkCJ2TPr7nT3hA/maxpreps-2019-20-boys-basketball-junior-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=April 27, 2020 |date=March 30, 2020}}</ref> Banchero was named to the [[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]] and [[Jordan Brand Classic]] rosters.<ref>{{Cite named to McDonald's All-America team|last=Joyce|first=Nathan|date=February 23, 2021|publisher=[[The Seattle Times]]|access-date=September 22, 2021}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Banchero was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2021 class. Although he received offers from top [[NCAA Division I]] programs, including [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] and [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], most recruiting analysts predicted that he would commit to [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]].<ref name="parrish">{{cite web |last1=Parrish |first1=Gary |title=Duke, Kentucky and UNC are recruiting Paolo Banchero, but family ties to Washington make his choice tough |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/duke-kentucky-and-unc-are-recruiting-paolo-banchero-but-family-ties-to-washington-make-his-choice-tough/ |work=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=April 26, 2020 |date=July 31, 2019}}</ref> Despite the predictions, on August 20, 2020, Banchero committed to playing college basketball for Duke.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29707146/duke-gets-commitment-center-paolo-banchero?platform=amp|title=Duke gets commitment from Paolo Banchero|last=Medcalf|first=Myron|date=August 20, 2020|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=June 13, 2021}}</ref>

==College career==
In his college debut, a 79–71 win against [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], Banchero scored 22 points.<ref>{{cite news |title=Coach K wins Garden finale as Duke tops Kentucky 79-71 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401369850 |access-date=November 10, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 9, 2021}}</ref> On November 15, Banchero earned his first [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) Freshman of the Week honor.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2021/11/15/athlete-awards-nc-states-seabron-dukes-banchero-earn-accs-first-weekly-honors-of-season.aspx|title=NC State's Seabron, Duke's Banchero Earn First ACC Weekly Honors of Season|date=November 15, 2021|publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|access-date=November 15, 2021}}</ref> On November 23, 2021, Banchero scored 28 points and 8 rebounds in a 107–81 victory against the Citadel.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://goduke.com/news/2021/11/23/mens-basketball-banchero-moore-lead-no-5-duke-past-the-citadel-107-81.aspx#:~:text=DURHAM%20%E2%80%93%20Freshman%20Paolo%20Banchero%20and,night%20at%20Cameron%20Indoor%20Stadium.&text=Banchero%20set%20career%20highs%20with,two%20steals%20and%20no%20turnovers.|title=Banchero, Moore Lead No.5 Duke Past The Citadel, 107–81|website=GoDuke.com|publisher=[[Duke Blue Devils]]|access-date=November 23, 2021}}</ref> He was named first-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] as well as [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|ACC Rookie of the Year]].<ref name="ACCAwards">{{cite press release |url=https://theacc.com/news/2022/3/6/athlete-awards-acc-unveils-2021-22-mens-basketball-awards.aspx |title=ACC Unveils 2021-22 Men's Basketball Awards |publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] |date=March 7, 2022 |accessdate=March 7, 2022}}</ref> On March 15, 2022, Banchero was named a [[2022 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|Third Team All-American]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-wisconsin-indiana-georgia-basketball-cffd2113c69053c28aa220a71ca94d69|title = The Associated Press Men's All-America Teams|website = [[Associated Press]]|date = 15 March 2022}}</ref> During the [[2022 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2022 NCAA tournament]], Banchero performed well, including scoring 22 points against [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Texas Tech vs. Duke - Box Score - March 24, 2022 - ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401408624 |access-date=2022-03-27 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> As a freshman, he averaged 17.2 points, 7.8 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game. On April 20, 2022, Banchero declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|title=Paolo Banchero to declare for NBA draft after one season with Duke Blue Devils|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33774305/paolo-banchero-declare-nba-draft-one-season-duke-blue-devils|date=April 20, 2022|accessdate=April 20, 2022}}</ref>

==National team career==
Banchero was eligible to play for the [[Italy national basketball team]] and indicated he wants to represent Italy in international competitions.<ref>{{cite news |title=Paolo Banchero: 'I'm excited to play for Italy' |url=https://basketnews.com/news-160608-paolo-banchero-im-excited-to-play-for-italy.html |access-date=18 May 2022 |work=basketnews.com |language=en}}</ref> He was selected to the country's 24-man squad for the [[EuroBasket 2022]] qualification games in November 2020, however he did not play.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ambitious Banchero waits in the wings for Italy |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/qualifiers/news/ambitious-banchero-waits-in-the-wings-for-italy |access-date=18 May 2022 |work=FIBA.basketball |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Banchero's mother, [[Rhonda Banchero|Rhonda]] (née Smith), played college basketball for [[Washington Huskies women's basketball|Washington]], leaving as the program's all-time scoring leader. She was a third-round selection in the [[2000 WNBA draft]] and played professionally in the [[American Basketball League (1996–1998)|American Basketball League]] and overseas, before becoming a basketball coach at [[Holy Names Academy]] in Seattle.<ref name=mother/><ref name=allen/> Banchero's father, Mario, and his uncle played [[college football]] for [[Washington Huskies football|Washington]]. His parents met while attending the [[University of Washington]].<ref name=parrish/> 

Banchero is of African-American descent on his mother’s side and is of Italian descent on his father's side.<ref name=bennett/> In February 2020, he received Italian citizenship.<ref name="evans">{{cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Jayda |title=First, state for O'Dea's Paolo Banchero. Next, the world? |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/star-times-boys-basketball-first-state-for-odeas-paolo-banchero-next-the-world/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |access-date=April 26, 2020 |date=March 2, 2020}}</ref>

Banchero's cousin on the Italian side, [[Chris Banchero]], plays basketball in the [[Philippine Basketball Association|PBA]].<ref>{{Citation |title=PAANO Na-Impluwensyahan Ni Chris Banchero Si Paolo Sa Basketball |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=utN9_TvuWyw |language=en |access-date=2022-06-20}}</ref> They both won championships at O'Dea High School.

On the morning of November 14, 2021, Banchero was charged with aiding and abetting [[Driving under the influence|DWI]] after [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] teammate Michael Savarino, grandson of coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]], was arrested on DWI charges. He is due to appear in court at a later date.<ref name="Borzello">{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Duke basketball player Michael Savarino, grandson of coach Mike Krzyzewski, faces DWI charges along with Paolo Banchero |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/32643987/duke-basketball-player-michael-savarino-grandson-coach-mike-krzyzewski-face-dwi-charges-paolo-banchero/ |work=[[ESPN]] |access-date=November 16, 2021 |date=November 16, 2021}}</ref>
